judgments.reasoning_cat1: Badly garbled in this text, but the substance — a successor Architect against whom the Contractor has no reasonable objection, with the same status under the Contract Documents — is definite. The garbling is the chief source of uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.1.2 and the Agreement's identification of the Architect; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Describes the Architect as the Owner's representative during construction and until final payment, with authority 'only to the extent provided in the Contract Documents, unless otherwise modified in writing'. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 1.1.2.1, which requires the Owner's express written consent alongside every Architect approval and disclaims Owner responsibility for means and methods; the Owner is inserted into a role this clause assigns to the Architect. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A disclaimer of Architect responsibility for the Contractor's failures and for acts of the Contractor and Subcontractors. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.2.1, 4.2.7 and 3.3.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires communications to run through the Architect 'except as otherwise provided in the Contract Documents or when direct communications have been specially authorized'. The exceptions are broad but signposted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 1.1.2.1 (every Architect communication must also go to the Owner in writing) and 2.1.1.1 (Owner's authorized representatives); the routing rule here and the parallel-notice rule there are hard to run together. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fragmentary in this text; the operative content is the Architect's evaluation of Applications and certification of amounts due. Little to construe beyond the truncation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.4.1-9.4.2 and Agreement 12.1.9/12.2.3; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Review is 'only for the limited purpose of checking for conformance with information given and the design concept expressed', and expressly not for 'the accuracy and completeness of other details such as dimensions and quantities'. The limits are stated with care.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.12.4-3.12.8 and Supplementary Conditions 3.12.7.1; the limitation is consistently repeated. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short authority provision for Change Orders, Construction Change Directives and minor changes. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 7.2.1 (Change Order signed by Owner, Contractor and Architect), 7.3.1 and Supplementary Conditions 7.1.3.1; consistent in outline. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fragmentary but substantively a duty to determine Substantial Completion dates, receive written warranties and issue the final Certificate. Definite in substance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.2.3 (whose time periods expressly supersede A201 9.4.1) and Supplementary Conditions 9.10.1.1 (no final Certificate until the Owner accepts all warranties); the certification conditions are set in three places. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Optional project representatives whose duties 'shall be as set forth in an exhibit to be incorporated in the Contract Documents' — an exhibit that does not exist here. A modest gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement Article 15's enumeration, which lists no such exhibit; the referenced document was never created. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Interpretations on written request 'within any time limits agreed upon or otherwise with reasonable promptness', with delay not recognised until 15 days after written request. The two timing standards sit oddly together but each is stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.3.7 and 8.3.1 (delay claims); the 15-day rule dovetails with the claims machinery. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Interpretations 'will be consistent with the intent of and reasonably inferable from the Contract Documents' and the Architect 'will not be liable for results of interpretations or decisions so rendered in good faith'. 'Reasonably inferable' and 'good faith' are both open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 1.2.1 and 4.4.5; the standards match. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Architect's decisions on matters relating to aesthetic effect will be final if consistent with the intent expressed in the Contract Documents' — 'aesthetic effect' and the conditional 'if consistent' both leave the finality genuinely uncertain. Nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 1.1.2.1, which reserves rights to the Owner expressly 'for purposes of aesthetic and cost control of the Work', and against 4.6.1, which excludes aesthetic-effect Claims from arbitration; who has the last word on aesthetics is answered differently in two places. Real conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines a Claim as a demand or assertion 'seeking, as a matter of right, adjustment or interpretation of Contract terms, payment of money, extension of time or other relief', and adds 'other disputes and matters in question ... arising out of or relating to the Contract'. The residual 'other relief' and the breadth of 'relating to' are the soft points.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.3.2 (21-day initiation), 4.4 and 4.6.1; the definition drives the whole dispute machinery consistently. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 21-day limit running from the occurrence 'or within 21 days after the claimant first recognizes the condition giving rise to the Claim, whichever is later' — a subjective recognition trigger inside a short forfeiture period. Genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.2.4 (a separate 30-day arbitration demand period) and 4.4.6 and 4.6.3; several different limitation periods govern overlapping subject matter. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires both parties to continue performing and paying pending resolution 'except as otherwise agreed in writing or as provided in Subparagraph 9.7.1 and Article 14'. The exceptions are identified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.7.1 (stop-work right) and 2.2.1 (evidence of financial arrangements as 'a condition precedent to commencement or continuation of the Work'); 2.2.1 supplies a stopping right this clause does not except. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on conditions that 'differ materially' from those indicated, or unknown conditions 'of an unusual nature' differing materially from those 'ordinarily found to exist and generally recognized as inherent in construction activities of the character provided for'. Every operative term is an evaluative standard — a classic differing-site-conditions dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 1.2.1.1(b) ('no extra charge or compensation ... on account of differences between actual dimensions and the dimensions indicated'), 4.3.2 and 8.3.1; the supplement narrows the equitable-adjustment route this clause opens. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Claims for additional cost may be brought 'for reasons including but not limited to' seven enumerated items ending with '(7) other reasonable grounds' — an explicit general catch-all after enumerated specifics, doubled by 'including but not limited to'. Precisely the general-versus-specific defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 7.1.3.1, which bars any claim to an increase founded on course of conduct or unjust enrichment; a wide-open 'other reasonable grounds' route and a strict Change-Order-only rule pull apart. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires written notice, an estimate of cost and probable effect, and only one Claim for a continuing delay. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 4.3.7.3 and 4.3.7.4, which add content requirements and bar separate increases for concurrent delays; cumulative. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Weather claims require data showing conditions 'were abnormal for the period of time, could not have been reasonably anticipated and had an adverse effect on the scheduled construction'. Three evaluative tests, all open — though the burden is clearly placed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 8.3.1 and Supplementary Conditions 4.3.7.3/4.3.7.4; consistent as a specific application. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires notice of injury or damage 'within a reasonable time not exceeding 21 days after discovery', with 'sufficient detail to enable the other party to investigate'. A capped reasonableness standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.3.2 and 10.2.5; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Unit prices are equitably adjusted where quantities are 'materially changed' so that application would 'cause substantial inequity'. 'Materially' and 'substantial inequity' are the nameable open standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 5.2.3, where the unit-price entry is blank, and 7.3.3.2; with no unit prices stated or subsequently agreed, the clause has nothing to adjust. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mutual consequential-damages waiver with two enumerated lists and a carve-out for 'anticipated profit arising directly from the Work' and for liquidated direct damages. The carve-outs are where the line between direct and consequential loss becomes genuinely arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 14.4.3, which entitles the Contractor on convenience termination to 'reasonable overhead and profit on the Work not executed', against Agreement 13.1's cap and 9.7.1's shutdown and start-up costs; the waiver says it applies 'without limitation, to all consequential damages due to either party's termination in accordance with Article 14', which cuts against those entitlements. Real conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A menu of five actions the Architect may take within ten days, including advising the parties it 'is unable to resolve the Claim' in the Architect's 'sole discretion'. Clear as a procedure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.4.5, 4.4.6 and 4.6.1 (Architect's decision as a condition precedent to arbitration); the sequence coheres. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive consultation power ('may, but shall not be obligated to'). Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.4.2 and 4.4.4; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A ten-day response requirement with three permitted responses. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.4.2 and 4.4.5; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The approval or rejection of a Claim by the Architect shall be final and binding on the parties but subject to mediation and arbitration' — a decision that is simultaneously final and reviewable. That internal tension is visible in the sentence itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.4.6 (30-day demand or the decision becomes final), 4.6.1 and Agreement 12.2.4 (Contractor may demand arbitration 'without a further decision of the Architect'); the conditions on finality are stated differently in each. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Finality attaches only where the Architect's written decision itself 'states that (1) the decision is final but subject to mediation and arbitration and (2) a demand ... must be made within 30 days'. Making the forfeiture depend on the Architect's own recital is a genuine trap, and the closing text is garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.4.5, 4.6.3 and Agreement 12.2.4, which also imposes a 30-day arbitration deadline on a different trigger; multiple overlapping forfeiture windows. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Badly garbled here; the substance is a permissive notice to the surety. Little operative content to construe apart from the damage to the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.4.1 (prior rights of the surety) and 14.2.2; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits a party to comply with lien notice or filing deadlines before resolution of a Claim. Narrow and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 12.1.4(b) and 12.2.2 (lien waivers and lien-free endorsement) and A201 9.10.2; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mediation is mandatory ('shall endeavor to resolve'), may be filed concurrently with an arbitration demand, and stays arbitration 'for a period of 60 days from the date of filing'. The garbled text obscures whether mediation is a genuine condition precedent — a question that turns on 'shall endeavor'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.6.1 ('shall, after decision by the Architect or 30 days ... be subject to arbitration' and 'prior to arbitration, the parties shall endeavor to resolve disputes by mediation') and Agreement 12.2.4, which allows an arbitration demand without a further Architect decision. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Equal sharing of the mediator's fee, mediation held where the Project is located, agreements enforceable as settlements. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.5.2 and 13.1.1 (governing law of the place of the Project); consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: All Claims are subject to arbitration 'except Claims relating to aesthetic effect and except those waived as provided for in Subparagraphs 4.3.10, 9.10.4 and 9.10.5', and only 'after decision by the Architect or 30 days after submission of the Claim to the Architect'. The stacked exceptions and the condition precedent are exactly what parties litigate about at the threshold.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.2.4 (arbitration 'without a further decision of the Architect'), 4.4.5-4.4.6, 4.5.2 (mediation) and 4.6.3; the routes into arbitration are described inconsistently across these provisions. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specifies AAA Construction Industry Arbitration Rules and the manner of filing a demand. Mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.6.1, 4.6.3 and Agreement 12.2.4; consistent as to forum, less so as to timing. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Demands must be within the 4.4.6/4.6.1 limits 'and in other cases within a reasonable time after the Claim has arisen', and never after the date when legal proceedings 'would be barred by the applicable statute of limitations as determined pursuant to Paragraph 13.7'. A reasonableness standard nested inside a statutory long-stop is genuinely hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 13.7.1's three accrual rules and Agreement 12.2.4; the limitation scheme depends on provisions that themselves fix accrual by reference to Substantial Completion and the final Certificate. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Bars consolidation and joinder except by written consent, then permits joinder of 'other persons substantially involved in a common question of fact or law whose presence is required if complete relief is to be accorded', excluding those whose interest 'is not substantial'. 'Substantially involved' and 'not substantial' are both open, and the provision is dense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.6.1-4.6.2 and 1.1.2 (no contractual relationship between Owner and Subcontractor or Architect and Contractor); the joinder limits track the no-privity structure. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The award rendered by the arbitrator or arbitrators shall be final, and judgment may be entered upon it.' Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.6.1-4.6.3 and 13.1.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of Subcontractor turning on a 'direct contract with the Contractor to perform a portion of the Work at the site', excluding separate contractors. Precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 6.1.2 and Agreement 10.1/12.1.8; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of Sub-subcontractor. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.1.1 and 9.6.2; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the Contractor to furnish proposed subcontractor names, with the Owner or Architect entitled to make 'reasonable objection' and failure to reply promptly constituting no objection. Clear procedure; 'promptly' is soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 10.1, under which the Owner may designate the persons from whom bids must be obtained and 'shall then determine ... which bids will be accepted'; that is an Owner-selects model against A201's Contractor-proposes model. Real conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A reciprocal prohibition on contracting with a person to whom either side has 'made reasonable and timely objection'. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 10.1's final sentence, which contains the same Contractor protection, and 10.2's Change Order remedy; consistent though duplicative. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adjusts the Contract Sum by 'the difference occasioned by such change', but denies any increase 'unless the Contractor has acted promptly and responsively in submitting names'. Both 'difference occasioned' and 'promptly and responsively' are open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 10.2, which gives the Contractor a Change Order for the bid differential when the Owner requires another bid to be accepted; the two adjustment routes overlap with different conditions. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line prohibition on changing a previously selected subcontractor over reasonable objection. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1-5.2.3; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A contingent assignment effective 'only after termination of the Contract by the Owner for cause' and only for accepted subcontracts, subject to the surety's prior rights. Conditions are clearly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 13.3 (Contractor must execute assignments as a condition of receiving payment) and 14.2.2.2; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Equitable adjustment of subcontractor compensation after a suspension exceeding 30 days. Short and definite; 'equitably adjusted' is the soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 14.3.2 and Agreement 13.4; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reserves the Owner's right to perform construction and award separate contracts, with the Contractor's remedy routed to Paragraph 4.3. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 6.1.3, 6.2.3 and Agreement 10.1; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A reading rule for the word 'Contractor' where separate contracts are awarded. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 6.1.1 and 5.1.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Owner coordinates separate contractors, and the construction schedule 'shall then constitute the schedules to be used by the Contractor, separate contractors and the Owner until subsequently revised' after 'joint review and mutual agreement'. The revision mechanism depends on agreement that may never come.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4/3.10.5, which give the Construction Schedule Contract Document status and a separate revision procedure; two schedule-revision regimes coexist. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deems the Owner subject to the same obligations and rights as the Contractor when performing with its own forces, 'including, without excluding others, those stated in Article 3, this Article 6 and Articles 10, 11 and 12'. The 'without excluding others' formula makes the list illustrative rather than exhaustive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 6.1.1 and 3.18.1 (indemnity running only from the Contractor); reciprocity is asserted generally but the indemnity is one-way. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires 'reasonable opportunity' for others' storage and activities and coordination 'as required by the Contract Documents'. Ordinary softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 6.1.3 and 3.13.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Failure to report discrepancies 'shall constitute an acknowledgment that the ... construction is fit and proper', 'except as to defects not then reasonably discoverable'. A deeming provision with a reasonableness exception — arguable but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.2.1-3.2.3 and Supplementary Conditions 1.2.1.1(b); consistent in approach. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Makes the Contractor liable to the Owner for costs payable to a separate contractor 'because of the Contractor's delays, improperly timed activities or defective construction', and the Owner reciprocally liable. 'Improperly timed' is the soft term; the reciprocity is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.3.10's consequential damages waiver, which waives many of the very losses this clause makes recoverable, and 6.1.3. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Prompt remedy of damage 'wrongfully caused' by the Contractor. Narrow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 10.2.5 and 3.14.2; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Extends the Contractor's cutting-and-patching responsibilities to the Owner and separate contractors. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.14.1-3.14.2; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Where a clean-up dispute arises the Owner may clean up 'and the Architect will allocate the cost among those responsible'. A unilateral allocation with no stated standard is the soft point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.4 (Architect's claim decisions subject to mediation and arbitration) and 3.15; the allocation is reviewable through the claims machinery. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Changes may be accomplished 'without invalidating the Contract, by Change Order, Construction Change Directive or order for a minor change in the Work'. Three routes, each defined elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 7.1.3.1, which says a change in the Contract Sum or Time 'shall be accomplished only by Change Order' except as permitted in 7.3 and 9.7.1 — omitting the 7.4 minor-change route this clause preserves. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines a Change Order as prepared by the Architect and signed by Owner, Contractor and Architect, stating agreement on three matters. Precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 7.1.3.1 and 7.2.3 and First Addendum 6.5; the tripartite signature requirement is the gateway those clauses depend on. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fragmentary line on methods for determining adjustments to the Contract Sum. Almost no operative text survives.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 7.3.3 and Agreement 6.1/6.2; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines a Construction Change Directive as prepared by the Architect and signed by Owner and Architect 'directing a change in the Work prior to agreement on adjustment' — a unilateral instrument. Its unilateral character is clear rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 7.1.3.1, which preserves 'Paragraph 7.3' as an exception to the Change-Order-only rule, and 7.3.8; consistent. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four alternative bases for adjustment including 'cost to be determined in a manner agreed upon by the parties and a mutually acceptable fixed or percentage fee' — an agreement-to-agree option and a fall-back to 7.3.6. The layered alternatives are workable but leave room.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 6.1-6.3, which map these terms onto the Cost of the Work and Contractor's Fee, and Agreement 5.2.3 (no unit prices stated); one of the four methods is unavailable. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the Contractor to proceed promptly on receipt of a Directive and advise of agreement or disagreement. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 7.3.5-7.3.8 and 4.3.3; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Signature by the Contractor converts a Directive into a Change Order effective immediately. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 7.2.1 and Supplementary Conditions 7.2.3 (Change Order as final settlement); consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: For deletions the allowance for overhead and profit is 'actual net cost as confirmed by the Architect', and where additions and credits are involved the allowance is figured on 'the basis of net increase, if any'. Netting rules are notoriously arguable, and 'covering related Work or substitutions' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 6.3-6.4, which redefine 'a reasonable allowance for overhead and profit' as the Contractor's Fee, a flat lump sum; a lump-sum fee cannot be netted per change. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allows costs under a Directive into Applications for Payment as an 'interim determination' pending final determination, 'subject to the right of either party to disagree and assert a claim'. Clear provisional structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 7.2.3, which makes agreement on any Change Order 'a final settlement of all matters relating to the change'; provisional pricing and final settlement are different regimes. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Agreement on adjustments is effective immediately and recorded by Change Order. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 7.2.1 and Supplementary Conditions 7.1.3.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Gives the Architect authority to order 'minor changes in the Work not involving adjustment in the Contract Sum or extension of the Contract Time and not inconsistent with the intent of the Contract Documents', binding on both parties. 'Minor' and 'not inconsistent with the intent' are the open terms, and a change that turns out to cost money is exactly where the fight starts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 7.1.3.1, which excepts only Paragraphs 7.3 and 9.7.1 from the Change-Order-only rule and not 7.4, and against Supplementary Conditions 1.2.1.1(c), which requires Owner and Architect approval of minor field changes. Real tension.
